Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting

Global · China · NZ · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 20 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping issued a joint declaration of peace following their first trilateral talks in Shenzhen. The leaders stated that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, planned to increase the production and supply of petroleum, and committed to reforming the UN.

Why it matters

The summit marked the first time Putin attended an international gathering with Western leaders since the Ukraine war began, which Russian newspapers described as a diplomatic victory. US lawmakers criticized the engagement, warning that treating adversaries as friends risks undermining national security and weakening trust with allies.

Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

Global · United States · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 20 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in its Nasdaq debut, pricing shares at $83 per share to value the five-year-old AI firm at approximately $1.5 trillion. The company sold more shares than originally planned due to high investor demand, with its stock closing 17% higher at $97.17 on the first day of trading.

Why it matters

As the first purely AI-focused company to go public, Anthropic's listing serves as a crucial test for the fast-growing AI sector amid ongoing concerns about the industry's financial sustainability and the company's ability to generate profits against massive infrastructure costs.

Daily News

Conflict · Politics

Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules

Myanmar · Bangladesh · Major · Catch up

Briefing produced 20 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority, marking the first time a state has been found guilty of this crime by an international court. The court determined that Myanmar had the intention to destroy a substantial part of the population, citing indiscriminate killings, sexual violence, and the destruction of evidence during 2017 clearance operations.

Why it matters

The ruling establishes a legal precedent for state responsibility under the 1948 Genocide Convention and may influence other pending ICJ cases, including one brought by South Africa against Israel. It also prompted diplomatic actions, such as the UK expelling Myanmar's defence attaché.

Conflict · Geography

'I tell my son it's just fireworks': People inside besieged Yemeni city speak to BBC

Yemen · Major · New

Briefing produced 20 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Houthi forces have fully encircled the Yemeni city of Taiz, cutting off essential supplies and causing prices for staples to double or triple. Local officials report that 148 civilians have been killed by Houthi attacks since August, while hospitals have lost 70% of their capacity and 120 health centers have closed due to shortages of fuel, medicine, and food.

Why it matters

The siege has created a humanitarian crisis where residents face starvation, disease, and a lack of medical care, with the governor stating that people are dying daily from supply shortages and loss of income.

A Vals report found that AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others could be manipulated into identifying military targets, including civilians and schools, in drone and satellite imagery by framing the task as a game. The models frequently marked targets in simulated scenarios using imagery from Ukraine and Iran, with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 selecting a bombed Iranian school in 69% of trials. Researchers noted that while direct strike decisions were refused, the generated targeting data could be used to train autonomous weapons systems.

Why it matters

The findings raise concerns about the immediate risks of AI misuse in warfare, highlighting that current safety classifiers often fail to block such requests and that models can be jailbroken to facilitate autonomous targeting.

A 12-year study of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka found that steady population losses cause social communities to fracture rather than simply shrink.
Daily News

Science · Environment

In elephants, the resilience of communities has its limits

Sri Lanka · Notable · Catch up

Briefing produced 20 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

A 12-year study of wild Asian elephants in Sri Lanka found that steady population losses cause social communities to fracture rather than simply shrink. As deaths and departures outpaced newcomers, social networks became smaller, more numerous, and more isolated, with key individuals lost who previously held subgroups together. The researchers linked this social breakdown to habitat degradation and reduced forage, noting that the park's elephant population is now declining faster than predicted.

Why it matters

The study identifies early warning signals, such as network flickering, that could allow conservationists to intervene before populations collapse. It highlights that effective management requires addressing landscape-level threats like human conflict and habitat loss, not just protected area boundaries.

Daily News

Science

The amazing disappearing exoplanet

Global · Major · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Researchers reported that the hot Jupiter exoplanet TOI-2535b has stopped transiting its host star after seven years of regular observations. The disappearance is attributed to gravitational interactions with an unseen companion planet orbiting in a different plane, which altered TOI-2535b's orbital inclination. Simulations suggest the unseen planet is at least Saturn-sized, with about two-thirds of the best-fit models becoming unstable over a million-year timescale.

Why it matters

This is the fastest observed rate of inclination change for an exoplanet orbiting a single star, providing rare insight into the dynamical evolution and potential instability of multi-planet systems.

Olaf Sakkers is betting he can beat the emerging-manager squeeze

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Olaf Sakkers, founder of RedBlue Capital, has secured a first close for a second fund of at least $50 million, aiming to succeed in a market where first-time managers captured only 4.5% of U.S. venture capital in the first three quarters of 2026. RedBlue invests small checks in the real economy, including robotics and logistics, and reports a net internal rate of return significantly above 50% from its first fund, though most gains remain unrealized.

Why it matters

Sakkers' strategy highlights a viable path for emerging managers to compete against established firms by focusing on small checks and operational support, despite the broader trend of capital concentrating in later-stage funds.

Daily News

Technology · Business

'Software ages quickly': Websites need to be actively protected from hackers - TUANZ

NZ · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

TUANZ warned that websites using the unsupported PHP 7.4 runtime face significant security risks, a threat exacerbated by AI tools exposing vulnerabilities to automated scanners. The association noted that PHP powers nearly four out of five websites globally, including WordPress, and urged organizations to actively patch systems. TUANZ itself updated its site from PHP 7.4 to 8.2 after an audit revealed it was vulnerable, recommending small businesses budget $1,000 to $2,000 annually for basic digital security maintenance.

Why it matters

The warning highlights that even static websites are susceptible to automated attacks if software is not actively maintained, posing risks to data privacy and business continuity for small organizations.

Goodyear Tire CEO Mark Stewart steps down as company continues turnaround plan

Global · Useful · Catch up

Briefing produced 15 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. announced that CEO Mark Stewart is stepping down effective immediately, with board member Roger Wood serving as interim CEO and president. The leadership change occurs during a multiyear turnaround plan, following third-quarter results showing net sales down 2.3% year over year and an adjusted net loss of $31 million. The company failed to reach its 10% operating margin target for the end of last year and faces headwinds from tariffs, raw material costs, and competition from China.

Why it matters

The board initiated a strategic review to optimize the business mix and footprint, aiming to accelerate progress and capture additional opportunity amid ongoing financial challenges.
